pr_body:
This switches IOStreams to use `pkg/term` from the go-gh library.

`term` does not handle most of what IOStreams did previously, so a lot of its logic still stays, but this cleans up overlapping functionality.

TODO:
- Bump go-gh to pull in https://github.com/cli/go-gh/pull/86

Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/6524
pr_comments:
> In the future do you invasion more of the iostreams package getting moved over to the term package?

I felt that iostreams was large (had too many responsibilities) and I didn't want to port it to go-gh verbatim; that's why I cherry-picked parts of it that felt "stable" and reusable. Some features that didn't make it:

- PAGER support
- Detecting terminal theme: this only makes sense if the extension uses pager _and_ Glamour or our `markdown` package
- Loading indicator (spinner) support: this isn't great as it requires manually starting & stopping spinner, which was historically error-prone
- Alternate screen buffer & clearing screen: this is relatively new to iostreams and we have to still check how successful it is
- `CanPrompt()` - only useful after we expose Survey functionality in go-gh
- `ReadUserFile()` - too specific
- `TempFile()` - too specific

Of all the things listed, I only see pager & spinner support as potential next extractions, but I feel neither are pressing and that they have to be redesigned (code-wise) as they're being ported over.

issue_context.title: `tablerow` in templates truncates strings
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

A clear and concise description of what the bug is. Include version by typing `gh --version`.

I have this code that makes a table of repo's issues:

```bash
start_timestamp=$(gdate --date="$(gdate +'%Y-%m-%d') - 1 month" +'%Y-%m-%d')
echo "Looking for issues closed since $start_timestamp -> closed.log"
gh issue list --search "is:closed closed:>$start_timestamp" --json 'title,url' \
  --template '{{range .}}{{tablerow .title .url}}{{end}}' > closed.log
```

(Here `gdate` is the GNU implementation of `date` from the `coreutils` package)

Just a month ago it used to make a table with full titles and URLs. But now `gh` truncates the strings, making the output basically useless:

```
Docs: table of content and language ...  https://github.com/tarantool/taranto...
Make separate customer zone pages fo...  https://github.com/tarantool/taranto...
```

I haven't found a way to revert to the previous behaviour in the following docs:

* https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_formatting
* https://docs.github.com/en/search-github/searching-on-github/searching-issues-and-pull-requests

gh version:
```
gh version 2.17.0 (2022-10-04)
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Run the code above on a repository with at least a few closed issues.
2. View the output in `closed.log`
3. See the title and URL strings truncated.

### Expected vs actual behavior

Same but in 3. you get full titles and URLs.

### Logs

(no extra logs needed)
comments:
Bisecting suggests the change came with 6a8deb1f5a9f2aa0ace2eb154523f3b9f23a05ae

---

To alleviate the problem, you could experiment with `--jq` or an environment variable.

1. --jq

```zsh
gh issue list --search "is:closed closed:>$start_timestamp" --json 'title,url' --jq '.[] | .title + "\t" + .url' > closed.log
```

2. Environment Variable

```zsh
GH_FORCE_TTY=100% gh issue list --search "is:closed closed:>$start_timestamp" --json 'title,url' \
  --template '{{range .}}{{tablerow .title .url}}{{end}}' > closed.log
```

EDIT:
3. printf
```zsh
gh issue list --search "is:closed closed:>$start_timestamp" --json 'title,url' --template '{{range .}}{{ printf "%s\t%s\n" .title .url}}{{end}}' > closed.log
```

Thanks @NickVolynkin for reporting and @LangLangBart for tracking down. This is indeed a bug from https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/6084 and will be fixed by https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/6421.

Note that `tablerow` will still truncate table columns to make the whole table fit in the current terminal viewport. The bug is that the terminal width was incorrectly measured when stdout was redirected. But, with `tablerow` you are never safe from truncation. If you don't want truncation, you might want to avoid using `tablerow` and just output values directly.

The workaround to avoid truncation is to force a really wide terminal with `GH_FORCE_TTY=10000`

review_comments: To my knowledge, Windows typically doesn't advertise terminal features via the TERM environment variable, but it does expose them programmatically through Console APIs. Hence, if we successfully enabled virtual terminal processing via these APIs, I think we can safely assume that alternate screen buffers are enabled. This is why the check isn't symmetrical with non-Windows platforms.
